entries.proposition: System: Ndufs4 knockout mice (complex I; Leigh syndrome model) and wild-type C57BL/6 mice given oral HypoxyStat, a haemoglobin left-shifter; the lever is tissue hypoxia in a mitochondrial disease. WWOX is not studied.
entries.snippet: This model lacks an essential complex 1 subunit of the electron transport chain (ETC) and reproduces the pathology of Leigh syndrome

entries.proposition: The authors state intermittent hypoxia or sleeping in hypoxia would be insufficient for mitochondrial disease; continuous hypoxia was judged necessary.
entries.snippet: making intermittent hypoxia or approaches such as “sleeping in hypoxia” insufficient

entries.proposition: The authors say gas-based devices carry fatal risk if equipment fails, which motivated the drug route.
entries.snippet: these devices carry significant risks, as equipment malfunctions could result in dangerously low-oxygen levels and potential fatalities

entries.proposition: Human data cited: a phase 1 inhaled hypoxia study took patients to about 85 percent arterial saturation and was well tolerated.
entries.snippet: Patients were gradually acclimated to hypoxic conditions until they reached an arterial oxygen saturation (SaO2) of ~85%.

entries.proposition: Pharmacology: HypoxyStat shifts the dissociation curve (p50 down about 82 percent) and has an effective half-life of 121 h in mice.
entries.snippet: we observed an effective half-life of 121 h and a blood/plasma ratio of 396 at 3 days post dosing

entries.proposition: Haemoglobin occupancy estimates are 29.3 percent at 200 mg/kg and 41.4 percent at 600 mg/kg; the dose used for efficacy was 400 mg/kg daily.
entries.snippet: we estimated Hb occupancy to be 29.3% at 200 mg/kg and 41.4% at 600 mg/kg

entries.proposition: Haematocrit and erythropoietin rose with dose, the known adaptive consequence of chronic hypoxia.
entries.snippet: we observed substantial increases in both Epo and hematocrit as HypoxyStat doses were increased

entries.proposition: Efficacy: daily dosing gave a 3 to 4 fold lifespan extension in Ndufs4 knockout mice, every other day 1.5 to 2 fold; the cohorts are n = 6, 9 and 9.
Late-stage start: dosing started at about P50 in the text; the Figure 5 legend gives 'late stages of disease (P80)' and the Methods say a single dose at about P55.
entries.snippet: initiating daily HypoxyStat treatment at P50 significantly extended the lifespan of these late-stage Ndufs4 KO mice

entries.proposition: Methods date the late-stage start at about postnatal day 55, a third value for the same experiment.
entries.snippet: For the reversal study, KO mice were dosed once with 200mg/kg on postnatal day ~P55, followed by 400mg/kg daily.

entries.proposition: Safety limits stated: the effect is covalent and cannot be acutely reversed except by transfusion; chronic hypoxia can cause pulmonary hypertension and right heart failure.
entries.snippet: However, the covalent nature of the drug-binding also means that this effect cannot be acutely reversed.

entries.proposition: Pulmonary hypertension risk of chronic hypoxia is named as an open long-term safety question.
entries.snippet: chronic hypoxia is known to cause pulmonary hypertension, which can lead to right heart failure

entries.proposition: Stated limitation: one disease model, mouse and in-vitro safety only, a first-generation compound.
entries.snippet: Moreover, our current safety studies are primarily in mice or in vitro.

entries.proposition: The authors say patients with milder electron-transport defects would need lower doses, and the required degree of hypoxia may differ between species.
entries.snippet: the exact degree of hypoxia required may differ between humans and mice

entries.proposition: Conflict declaration: the senior author consulted for Maze Therapeutics and has hypoxia-therapy patents; the work was supported by a sponsored research agreement with Maze Therapeutics.
entries.snippet: I.H.J. was previously a consultant for Maze Therapeutics and has patents related to hypoxia therapy.

entries.proposition: Figures 1 to 3: oxygen-dissociation curves with p50 about 26 (vehicle), 7.2 (GBT-440) and 5.6 (HypoxyStat); GBT-440 survival and temperature rescue absent (n = 6 and 9); PK curves; haematocrit up to about 59 percent at 600 mg/kg and plasma Epo about 80 pg/mL; head-to-head: HypoxyStat Epo about 380 pg/mL against about 130 for 11 percent oxygen, haematocrit about 52 against about 48 percent, hindbrain HIF targets induced to similar fold.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 1D p50 table 7.2 5.6 26.0 25.7; Figure 2B GBT-440 survival; Figure 3D hematocrit bars to about 59; Figure 3F Epo; Figure 3H VEGFA ACER2 ADM ANGPT2 DEPP1.

entries.proposition: Figures 4 to 6: survival (vehicle ends about day 65; 48 h dosing about day 120; 24 h dosing to about day 190 with early deaths in some animals); neuropathology with Iba1-positive lesions in the vestibular region of vehicle knockouts; behaviour and temperature bars; reversal survival (vehicle n = 6, late treatment n = 10, last death about day 170), reversal body weight, before (P50) and after (P80) comparisons; Figure 6 is a mechanism cartoon.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 4 A-E, Figure 5 A-D, Figure 6 schematic.
